journey.title: Focus stays in the results dialog after Show all removes itself
journey.goal: Activating a control that removes itself keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

functionalJourney.title: Show all results with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, lists every result and closes

guards.title: Escape closes results and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: When the focused button inside the dialog is removed by its click handler, focus leaves the dialog and the focus-trap's checkFocusIn attempts to restore focus to the previously focused node, which is now detached, resulting in focus not being restored inside the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify checkFocusIn to verify that the most recently focused node is still connected and focusable before attempting to refocus it; otherwise fallback to the initial focus node (or first tabbable node) within the trap.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the dialog after activating a control that removes itself, ensuring users can continue navigating via Tab/Shift+Tab without escaping.
functional_risks: Altered focus restoration logic might affect edge cases where a detached node is legitimately the intended restore target (unlikely).
Additional isFocusable check may introduce minimal performance overhead.
If isFocusable throws for certain nodes, the guard prevents exceptions but may cause unexpected fallback.
verification_requirements: After clicking 'Show all 4 results', pressing Tab should move focus to the next focusable element inside the dialog (e.g., first list item).
Escape key should still close the dialog and return focus to the opener button.
Opening the dialog should still place initial focus on the close button.
Removing other focusable elements inside the dialog should not break the trap's ability to retain focus.

plan.root_cause: When the focused 'Show all 4 results' button is removed by its click handler, focus leaves the dialog and the focus-trap's checkFocusIn attempts to restore focus to the previously focused node (now detached). The tabbable node cache is stale, so getInitialFocusNode may not reflect the current DOM, and the detached node's focus() call does nothing, leaving focus on the body.
plan.repair_strategy: Update the tabbable node cache in checkFocusIn before attempting focus restoration, and verify the most recently focused node is still connected and focusable; otherwise fall back to the initial focus node (first tabbable node in the updated cache).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the dialog after activating a control that removes itself, ensuring users can continue navigating via Tab/Shift+Tab without escaping.
functional_risks: Calling updateTabbableNodes on every focus escape adds minimal overhead (rare event).
If isFocusable throws for certain nodes, the guard prevents exceptions but may cause unexpected fallback.
Altered focus restoration logic might affect edge cases where a detached node is legitimately the intended restore target (unlikely).
verification_requirements: After clicking 'Show all 4 results', pressing Tab should move focus to the next focusable element inside the dialog (e.g., first list item or close button).
Escape key should still close the dialog and return focus to the opener button.
Opening the dialog should still place initial focus on the close button.
Removing other focusable elements inside the dialog should not break the trap's ability to retain focus.

plan.root_cause: When the focused 'Show all 4 results' button (#more) is removed by its click handler, focus leaves the dialog and the focus trap's checkFocusIn handler attempts to restore focus to the previously focused node (now detached). The existing fallback to getInitialFocusNode() may not reliably select a currently focusable node because the tabbable cache update timing or node connectivity checks fail in the test environment, leaving focus on the body element.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify checkFocusIn to immediately refresh the tabbable node cache and directly target the first tabbable node in the primary container group when focus escapes, bypassing the detached-node restoration logic entirely. This ensures a valid, connected focus target is selected from the current DOM state.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the dialog after activating a control that removes itself, ensuring users can continue navigating via Tab/Shift+Tab without escaping to the body element.
functional_risks: Focus restoration now always targets the first tabbable node (close button) rather than the previously focused position, which may surprise users expecting focus to return near their last position.
If the first tabbable node is not the desired initial focus (e.g., initialFocus option specified), the fallback may not respect that option in escape scenarios.
Minimal performance overhead from updateTabbableNodes on focus escape (rare event).
verification_requirements: After clicking 'Show all 4 results', pressing Tab should move focus to the next focusable element inside the dialog (e.g., first list item or close button).
Escape key should still close the dialog and return focus to the opener button.
Opening the dialog should still place initial focus on the close button.
Removing other focusable elements inside the dialog should not break the trap's ability to retain focus.
